• 15‑64 yrs: **≈ 67.5 %** (≈ 936 m)
• 65 + yrs: **≈ 6.8 %** (≈ 95 m) | Wikipedia | | **Projected growth trend** | Population will rise to about **1.7 billion by 2050** (UN medium‑projection) | Wikipedia & UN World Population Prospects | | **Historical milestone** | India surpassed China in mid‑2023, becoming the world’s most populous country. | Al Jazeera (UNFPA estimate, 19 Apr 2023) | | **Population share of world** | **≈ 1/6** of the global population (~ 18 %) | Wikipedia | --- ### Quick overview * **Current size** – India’s population is just over 1.44 billion (mid‑2023), a figure that has surpassed China’s for the first time in modern history. * **Growth** – The country’s growth rate has steadily fallen from the high‑twenty percent rates of the 1960s to just under 1 % today, reflecting lower fertility, higher life expectancy, and a rapidly aging cohort. * **Demographic dividend** – Roughly two‑thirds of the population (15‑64 yrs) are of working age, offering a potential economic advantage, though this dividend will peak and then decline as the population ages. * **Future outlook** – UN medium‑projections place India’s population at ~1.7 billion by 2050, after which growth will slow sharply. By 2100, the estimate is ~1.5

**China’s Population – Current Status, Recent Trends, and Future Outlook**

| Indicator | 2024 (latest official data) | 2023 | 2022 | Notes |
|-----------|-----------------------------|------|------|-------|
| **Total population** | **1 408 280 000** (≈1.408 billion) | 1 409 670 000 | 1 411 750 000 | Declining for the 3rd consecutive year【Wikipedia‑2024】 |
| **Natural growth rate** | –0.99 ‰ | –1.48 ‰ | –0.60 ‰ | Decline due to falling fertility and aging population【Wikipedia‑2024】 |
| **Birth rate** | 6.77 ‰ | 6.39 ‰ | 6.77 ‰ | Lowest since 2012; 9.54 million births in 2024【Wikipedia‑2024】 |
| **Death rate** | 7.76 ‰ | 7.87 ‰ | 7.37 ‰ | 10.93 million deaths in 2024, rising as population ages【Wikipedia‑2024】 |
| **Sex ratio (males / females)** | 51.1 % / 48.9 % | 51.1 % / 48.9 % | 51.1 % / 48.9 % | Slight male‑preference persists, but close to parity【Wikipedia‑2024】 |
| **Urban share** | 67 % (≈943 million) | 67 % | 67 % | Continuing urbanisation, but growth slowing【Wikipedia‑2024】 |
| **Population aged 60 +** | 310 million (22 %) | 296 million | 280 million | Rapid ageing; projected >400 million by 2035【Reuters‑2024】 |
| **Age‑specific fertility (TFR)** | 1.06 (2023 estimate) | 1.06 | 1.07 | Far below replacement level (2.1)【UN‑2024】 |

### Key Drivers of the Recent Decline

1. **Very low fertility** – The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) has stayed below replacement since the 1990s, falling to 1.06 in 2023.  
2. **Increasing mortality** – With a rapidly ageing cohort, deaths have risen sharply (7.87 ‰ in 2023, 7.76 ‰ in 2024).  
3. **COVID‑19 impact** – The 2022‑23 surge in deaths (10 million+ deaths in 2024) contributed to the natural decline.  
4. **Limited effect of policy changes** – The one‑child policy ended in 2016, but its demographic legacy still lingers.

### Age Structure (End‑2024)

- **0‑14 years:** ~222 million (≈15.8 %)  
- **15‑59 years:** ~875

**India vs. China – Population snapshot (mid‑2024)**  

| Item | India | China | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|-------|
| **Total population** | ≈ 1 451 million (mid‑2024) | 1 408 million (2024 official) | India is ~43 million larger |
| **Population share of world** | ~19 % | ~19 % | Both account for roughly one‑sixth of the global population |
| **Growth rate (natural)** | +0.89 % per year (2023) | –0.099 % per year (2024) | India continues to grow, China is in decline |
| **Birth rate** | 16.15 per 1 000 (2023) | 6.77 per 1 000 (2024) | China’s birth rate is less than half India’s |
| **Death rate** | 9.10 per 1 000 (2023) | 7.76 per 1 000 (2024) | India still has a higher death rate, but the gap is narrowing |
| **Median age** | 28 years | ~
